overview: This file traces the deepening crisis in Japanese agriculture from 1930 to 1938, with its core documentation focused on the Depression years of 1932–1933. U.S. diplomatic reports, departmental memoranda, translated Japanese newspaper articles, and file notes describe collapsing crop and silk prices, crushing rural debt, tenant-landlord tensions, farmers’ political mobilization, and fears of sporadic violence or agrarian revolution. The records also examine military involvement in rural relief, debates over inflationary government assistance, and three agrarian laws enacted in 1933 to address credit and structural problems. Later documents broaden the subject to restrictions on foreign exploitation of Japanese land and natural resources and an individual proposal to use hydroponics to alleviate food scarcity and encourage an end to the war in China.
interest: American diplomats' readings of rural distress, mobilization and militarism, disputed agrarian-revolution reports, and the 1938 hydroponics proposal.
